name: PassRole viability fails CLOSED on non-canonical same-account ARN spellings (S2-passrole-allstmts, ARN-spelling axis)
note: Same CLASS of fail-open as the statement-ORDER demotion, reached through ARN SPELLING instead of ordering. A PassRole target ARN's partition/account tokens are extracted with a lenient case-insensitive regex but were compared for same-vs-cross account with EXACT string equality. So a role in the subject's OWN account written with a non-canonical spelling - uppercase/mixed-case partition, embedded whitespace/tab, a space after a colon, or a non-12-digit account token - failed the exact match, was judged cross-account/cross-partition NOT-viable, demoted critical->medium (PASSROLE_CROSS_ACCOUNT_INCOMPATIBLE / PARTITION_MISMATCH) and slipped under the default 'high' exit gate to exit 0 CLEAN - order-independent, no decoy needed. FIX: an unmodelable partition/account token (partition not a recognized AWS partition, account not a bare 12-digit id, once wildcards are excluded) yields UNKNOWN viability that fails CLOSED via requiredUnknowns (scan -> exit 3), and the engine keeps the finding at critical (never a below-threshold medium). Each `variant` is a single-Pass policy; scan() must NEVER return exit 0 CLEAN and analyze() must NOT emit a confident cross-account/partition demotion. The `orderings` block additionally proves the fix is statement-ORDER-independent: a canonical cross-account decoy sorted before OR after an unmodelable same-account grant must still fail closed in every permutation.
